why: The Bean rulings in setting-registry.json's `bean_rulings*` metadata reclassified
several setting keys away from the automated Phase-1 conclusion. The upstream
rewritten, so they still carry the ORIGINAL classification. That state is
DELIBERATE and accepted — it is not a live inconsistency, because the golden
master is not currently regenerated from those artefacts.
This file records exactly that accepted state so the guard can be BLOCKING
without failing the build on the known-good baseline. The guard fails on any
DIFFERENCE from this file in either direction:
* a NEW or INCREASED (file, key, count) triple  -> a regeneration is adding
references and is about to revert a ruling;
* an accepted line whose upstream references are GONE or REDUCED -> the drift
was fixed upstream and this baseline line is now obsolete and must be
deleted, otherwise the baseline rots into permanent blindness.
_meta.keyed_on: count, NOT mere presence — adding a 3rd `css:stroke` row to setting-types.json trips the gate even though the (file, key) pair is already accepted.
_meta.seeded: 2026-08-06, from a live run of check-reclassified-keys.py against this tree.
_meta.do_not: Do NOT add a line here to silence a genuine regeneration. Fix the upstream artefact, or carry the ruling forward in whatever regenerates the golden master.
_meta.dispositionVocabularyNote: Closed vocabulary: by-design (correct, will never need fixing) / accepted-debt (real gap, consciously deferred) / detector-limitation (the checker itself is wrong — flags a rule violation per THE-MIGRATION-METHOD.md:455, not a normal outcome) / blocked (waiting on something external). See .claude/parking.md P-BASELINE-DISPOSITION-VOCABULARY / .claude/LEDGER.md.
